# Side by side: everyday date/time code in five languages

<!-- Generated by tools/side_by_side.py from the UTV-first example tests. Do not edit by hand. -->

Each task shows how it is done with UTV in each language, exactly as the code appears in
that language's UTV-first example tests ([`example-tests.md`](example-tests.md)). Every test
says in its doc comment what the language's own date/time API does for the same task, and
computes its expected value with that API wherever the two agree. The same tasks seen from
the native side are in each library's native-first tests.

| Language | Tests | Native API compared |
|---|---|---|
| C# | `implementations/csharp/tests/Utv.Examples.Tests/UtvFirst/*.cs` | DateOnly, DateTime, DateTimeOffset, TimeZoneInfo |
| Java | `implementations/java/src/test/java/net/icelander/utv/examples/utvfirst/*.java` | java.time |
| Python | `implementations/python/tests/examples/utv_first/test_*.py` | datetime, zoneinfo |
| TypeScript | `implementations/typescript/test/examples/utv-first/*.test.ts` | Date, Intl |
| Rust | `implementations/rust/tests/utv_first/*.rs` | chrono, chrono-tz |

## 1. Now

### Now

**C#**

```csharp
/// <summary>
/// Verifies that CivilDateTime.FromDateTime returns unsupported when the DateTime's Kind is Local.
/// Compared with: <c>DateTime.Now</c> returns Kind Local, a wall time that only means something on this machine.
/// </summary>
[Fact]
public void Test_FromDateTime_ReturnsUnsupported_WhenTheKindIsLocal()
{
    // GIVEN: a reading shaped like DateTime.Now's, tied to this machine's zone
    DateTime givenLocalTime = new(2026, 11, 5, 14, 30, 0, DateTimeKind.Local);

    // WHEN
    Outcome<CivilDateTime> actualOutcome = CivilDateTime.FromDateTime(givenLocalTime);

    // EXPECTATIONS: refused, because the host's zone is hidden input
    UtvStatus expectedStatus = UtvStatus.Unsupported;
    string expectedCode = "local-zone";

    // THEN
    Assert.Equal(expectedStatus, actualOutcome.Status);
    Assert.Contains(expectedCode, actualOutcome.Diagnostics.Codes);
}

/// <summary>
/// Verifies that Instant.FromDateTimeOffset takes a clock reading as an input when the program reads the clock.
/// Compared with: <c>DateTimeOffset.UtcNow</c> reads the clock itself; UTV never does, so tests can fix "now".
/// </summary>
[Fact]
public void Test_FromDateTimeOffset_ReturnsTheSameMoment_WhenGivenAClockReading()
{
    // GIVEN: a clock reading, as DateTimeOffset.UtcNow would return it
    DateTimeOffset givenReading = new(2026, 11, 5, 13, 30, 0, 123, TimeSpan.Zero);

    // WHEN
    Instant actualNow = Instant.FromDateTimeOffset(givenReading);

    // EXPECTATIONS: the same moment, counted in milliseconds since 1970 as .NET counts it
    Instant expectedNow = Instant.FromUnixNanoseconds(givenReading.ToUnixTimeMilliseconds() * 1_000_000);

    // THEN
    Assert.Equal(expectedNow, actualNow);
}
```

**Java**

```java
/**
 * Verifies that Instant.from takes a clock reading as an input when the program reads the clock.
 * Compared with: {@code java.time.Instant.now()} reads the clock itself; UTV never does, so tests can fix "now".
 */
@Test
void returnsTheSameMoment_whenGivenAClockReading() {
    // GIVEN: a clock reading, as java.time.Instant.now() would return it
    java.time.Instant givenReading = java.time.Instant.parse("2026-11-05T13:30:00.123456789Z");

    // WHEN
    Instant actualNow = Instant.from(givenReading);

    // EXPECTATIONS: the same moment, counted as java.time counts it: seconds since 1970 and nanoseconds
    Instant expectedNow = Instant.fromUnixSeconds(givenReading.getEpochSecond(), givenReading.getNano());

    // THEN
    assertEquals(expectedNow, actualNow);
}

/**
 * Verifies that JavaTime.fromDate returns unsupported when asked for the wall time of a java.util.Date.
 * Compared with: {@code Date.toString()} and {@code LocalDateTime.now()} take the wall time from
 * {@code ZoneId.systemDefault()}, a zone that only means something on this machine.
 */
@Test
void returnsUnsupported_whenAskedForTheWallTime() {
    // GIVEN: a reading shaped like new Date()'s, whose fields come from the host's default zone
    Date givenReading = Date.from(java.time.Instant.parse("2026-11-05T13:30:00Z"));
    JavaTime.As givenIntent = JavaTime.As.LOCAL_DATE_TIME;

    // WHEN
    UtvResult actualResult = JavaTime.fromDate(givenReading, givenIntent);

    // EXPECTATIONS: refused, because the host's zone is hidden input
    Status expectedStatus = Status.UNSUPPORTED;
    String expectedCode = "local-zone";

    // THEN
    assertEquals(expectedStatus, actualResult.status());
    assertTrue(actualResult.diagnostics().stream().anyMatch(d -> d.code().equals(expectedCode)), actualResult.toJson().toString());
}
```

**Python**

```python
def test_returns_the_same_moment_when_given_a_clock_reading(self):
    """Verifies that Instant.from_unix_nanoseconds takes a clock reading as an input when the program reads the
    clock.

    Compared with: ``datetime.now(timezone.utc)`` reads the clock itself; UTV never does, so the caller passes
    ``time.time_ns()`` in and tests can fix "now".
    """
    # GIVEN: a clock reading, as time.time_ns() would return it
    given_reading = 1_793_885_400_123_000_000

    # WHEN
    actual_now = Instant.from_unix_nanoseconds(given_reading)

    # EXPECTATIONS: the same moment, counted in microseconds since 1970 as Python's datetime counts it
    tmp_native = datetime(1970, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc) + timedelta(microseconds=given_reading // 1_000)
    expected_now = from_native(tmp_native, Intent.INSTANT).single()

    # THEN
    self.assertEqual(expected_now, actual_now)

def test_returns_unsupported_when_a_naive_datetime_is_asked_for_an_instant(self):
    """Verifies that from_native returns unsupported when a naive datetime is to be read as an instant.

    Compared with: ``datetime.now()`` returns a naive wall time that only means something on this machine, and
    ``astimezone()`` would read it in this machine's zone.
    """
    # GIVEN: a reading shaped like datetime.now()'s, with no zone
    given_local_time = datetime(2026, 11, 5, 14, 30)
    given_intent = Intent.INSTANT

    # WHEN
    actual_outcome = from_native(given_local_time, given_intent)

    # EXPECTATIONS: refused, because the host's zone is hidden input
    expected_outcome_type = Unsupported
    expected_code = "local-zone"

    # THEN
    self.assertIsInstance(actual_outcome, expected_outcome_type)
    self.assertIn(expected_code, actual_outcome.codes)
```

```typescript
/**
 * Verifies that fromDate returns unsupported when asked for the Date's local wall time.
 * Compared with: `getHours()` and the other local methods read the host's time zone, so the same Date shows a
 * different wall time on every machine.
 */
it("returns unsupported when the intent is local", () => {
  // GIVEN: a reading as Date.now() would give it, and a request for its wall time on this machine
  const givenReading = new Date(1_793_885_400_123);
  const givenIntent = "local";

  // WHEN
  const actualResult: UtvResult = fromDate(givenReading, givenIntent);

  // EXPECTATIONS: refused, because the host's zone is hidden input; name a zone or an offset instead
  const expectedStatus = "unsupported";
  const expectedCodes = ["local-zone"];

  // THEN
  assert.equal(actualResult.status, expectedStatus);
  assert.deepEqual(actualResult.diagnostics.map((diagnostic) => diagnostic.code), expectedCodes);
});

/**
 * Verifies that Instant.fromUnixMilliseconds takes a clock reading as an input when the program reads the clock.
 * Compared with: `Date.now()` reads the clock itself; UTV never does, so tests can fix "now".
 */
it("returns the same moment when given a clock reading", () => {
  // GIVEN: a clock reading, as Date.now() would return it
  const givenReading = 1_793_885_400_123;

  // WHEN
  const actualNow: Instant = Instant.fromUnixMilliseconds(givenReading);

  // EXPECTATIONS: the same moment, as Date writes it
  const expectedText = new Date(1_793_885_400_123).toISOString();

  // THEN
  assert.equal(actualNow.toString(), expectedText);
});
```

**Rust**

```rust
/// Verifies that Instant::from_system_time takes a clock reading as an input when the program reads the clock.
/// Compared with: `Utc::now()` and `SystemTime::now()` read the clock themselves; UTV never does, so a test can
/// fix "now".
#[test]
fn returns_the_same_moment_when_given_a_clock_reading() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
    // GIVEN: a clock reading, as SystemTime::now() would return it: 13:30:00.123 UTC on 5 November 2026
    let given_reading: SystemTime = UNIX_EPOCH + Duration::new(1_793_885_400, 123_000_000);

    // WHEN
    let actual_now = Instant::from_system_time(given_reading);

    // EXPECTATIONS: the same moment, as chrono reads it from the same SystemTime
    let expected_now = Instant::try_from(DateTime::<Utc>::from(given_reading))?;

    // THEN
    assert_eq!(expected_now, actual_now);
    Ok(())
}

/// Verifies that interop::chrono::from_local returns unsupported whatever the `DateTime<Local>` holds.
/// Compared with: `Local::now()` returns a `DateTime<Local>`, a wall time that only means something on this
/// machine, so UTV offers no typed conversion from it at all.
///
/// Making the given value reads this machine's zone on purpose, because a `DateTime<Local>` cannot be made
/// without it; the outcome is the same for every zone and every moment.
#[test]
fn returns_unsupported_when_given_a_local_date_time() {
    // GIVEN: a reading shaped like Local::now()'s: 13:30 UTC on 5 November 2026, in this machine's zone
    let given_reading: DateTime<Local> = DateTime::from_timestamp(1_793_885_400, 0).unwrap().with_timezone(&Local);

    // WHEN
    let actual_result = from_local(given_reading);

    // EXPECTATIONS: refused, because the host's zone is hidden input
    let expected_status = Status::Unsupported;
    let expected_code = "local-zone";

    // THEN
    assert_eq!(expected_status, actual_result.status);
    assert!(actual_result.diagnostics.iter().any(|d| d.code == expected_code));
}
```

### 5 November 2026

**C#**

```csharp
/// <summary>
/// Verifies that CivilDate.Of creates the date when the fields name a real day.
/// Compared with: <c>new DateOnly(2026, 11, 5)</c> names the same day.
/// </summary>
[Fact]
public void Test_Of_CreatesTheDate_WhenTheFieldsNameARealDay()
{
    // GIVEN: 5 November 2026
    int givenYear = 2026;
    int givenMonth = 11;
    int givenDay = 5;

    // WHEN
    CivilDate actualDate = CivilDate.Of(givenYear, givenMonth, givenDay);

    // EXPECTATIONS: the same day as .NET's DateOnly
    CivilDate expectedDate = CivilDate.FromDateOnly(new DateOnly(2026, 11, 5));
    string expectedText = "2026-11-05";

    // THEN
    Assert.Equal(expectedDate, actualDate);
    Assert.Equal(expectedText, actualDate.ToString());
}
```

### Day of week and ISO week

**C#**

```csharp
/// <summary>
/// Verifies that CivilDate.DayOfWeek returns the weekday of the date.
/// Compared with: <c>DateOnly.DayOfWeek</c> names the same day, but numbers Sunday 0 where ISO numbers it 7.
/// </summary>
[Fact]
public void Test_DayOfWeek_ReturnsThursday_WhenTheDateIs5November2026()
{
    // SYSTEM UNDER TEST: 5 November 2026
    CivilDate sut = CivilDate.Of(2026, 11, 5);

    // WHEN
    Weekday actualWeekday = sut.DayOfWeek;

    // EXPECTATIONS: the weekday .NET names for the same day
    string expectedName = new DateOnly(2026, 11, 5).DayOfWeek.ToString();

    // THEN
    Assert.Equal(expectedName, actualWeekday.ToString());
}

/// <summary>
/// Verifies that CivilDate.IsoWeek returns the ISO 8601 week number of the date.
/// Compared with: <c>ISOWeek.GetWeekOfYear</c> needs a <c>DateTime</c>, so a time of day is invented first.
/// </summary>
[Fact]
public void Test_IsoWeek_Returns45_WhenTheDateIs5November2026()
{
    // SYSTEM UNDER TEST: 5 November 2026
    CivilDate sut = CivilDate.Of(2026, 11, 5);

    // WHEN
    int actualWeek = sut.IsoWeek;

    // EXPECTATIONS: the ISO week .NET computes for midnight of the same day
    int expectedWeek = ISOWeek.GetWeekOfYear(new DateTime(2026, 11, 5));

    // THEN
    Assert.Equal(expectedWeek, actualWeek);
}
```

**Java**

```java

 * Verifies that CivilDate.dayOfWeek returns Thursday when the date is 5 November 2026.

    // WHEN

    // EXPECTATIONS: the ISO week java.time computes for the same day
    int expectedWeek = LocalDate.of(2026, 11, 5).get(IsoFields.WEEK_OF_WEEK_BASED_YEAR);

    // THEN
    assertEquals(expectedWeek, actualWeek);
}
```

```python
def test_returns_thursday_when_the_date_is_5_november_2026(self):
    """Verifies that CivilDate.day_of_week returns the weekday of the date, numbered as in ISO 8601.

    Compared with: ``date.isoweekday()`` numbers it the same, 4; ``date.weekday()`` would number it 3.
    """
    # SYSTEM UNDER TEST: 5 November 2026
    sut = CivilDate.of(2026, 11, 5)

    # WHEN
    actual_weekday = sut.day_of_week

    # EXPECTATIONS: the ISO weekday Python numbers for the same day
    expected_weekday = Weekday(date(2026, 11, 5).isoweekday())
    expected_name = "Thursday"

    # THEN
    self.assertEqual(expected_weekday, actual_weekday)
    self.assertEqual(expected_name, str(actual_weekday))

def test_returns_45_when_the_date_is_5_november_2026(self):
    """Verifies that CivilDate.iso_week returns the ISO 8601 week number of the date.

    Compared with: ``date.isocalendar().week`` gives the same week.
    """
    # SYSTEM UNDER TEST: 5 November 2026
    sut = CivilDate.of(2026, 11, 5)

    # WHEN
    actual_week = sut.iso_week

    # EXPECTATIONS: the ISO week Python computes for the same day
    expected_week = date(2026, 11, 5).isocalendar().week

    # THEN
    self.assertEqual(expected_week, actual_week)
```

```rust
/// Verifies that CivilDate::day_of_week returns the weekday of the date, numbered the ISO way.
/// Compared with: `NaiveDate::weekday` names the same day; its `number_from_monday` is the ISO number, while
/// `num_days_from_monday` counts from 0.
#[test]
fn returns_thursday_when_the_date_is_5_november_2026() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
    // SYSTEM UNDER TEST: 5 November 2026
    let sut = CivilDate::of(2026, 11, 5)?;

    // WHEN
    let actual_weekday = sut.day_of_week();

    // EXPECTATIONS: Thursday, the ISO number chrono gives for the same day
    let expected_weekday = Weekday::Thursday;
    let expected_number = NaiveDate::from_ymd_opt(2026, 11, 5).unwrap().weekday().number_from_monday();

    // THEN
    assert_eq!(expected_weekday, actual_weekday);
    assert_eq!(expected_number, actual_weekday.number());
    Ok(())
}

/// Verifies that CivilDate::iso_week returns the ISO 8601 week number of the date.
/// Compared with: `NaiveDate::iso_week().week()` gives the same week.

    // SYSTEM UNDER TEST: 5 November 2026
    let sut = CivilDate::of(2026, 11, 5)?;

    // WHEN
    let actual_week = sut.iso_week();

    // EXPECTATIONS: the ISO week chrono computes for the same day
    let expected_week = NaiveDate::from_ymd_opt(2026, 11, 5).unwrap().iso_week().week();

    // THEN
    assert_eq!(expected_week, actual_week);
    Ok(())
}
```

## 3. Invalid dates

### 30 February 2026

**C#**

```csharp
/// <summary>
/// Verifies that CivilDate.TryOf returns invalid when the day is 30 February.
/// Compared with: <c>new DateOnly(2026, 2, 30)</c> throws; TryOf reports the problem as a value instead.
/// </summary>
[Fact]
public void Test_TryOf_ReturnsInvalid_WhenTheDayIs30February()
{
    // GIVEN: 30 February 2026
    int givenYear = 2026;
    int givenMonth = 2;
    int givenDay = 30;

    // WHEN
    Outcome<CivilDate> actualOutcome = CivilDate.TryOf(givenYear, givenMonth, givenDay);

    // EXPECTATIONS: invalid, because February 2026 has 28 days
    UtvStatus expectedStatus = UtvStatus.Invalid;
    string expectedCode = "day-out-of-range";

    // THEN
    Assert.Equal(expectedStatus, actualOutcome.Status);
    Assert.Contains(expectedCode, actualOutcome.Diagnostics.Codes);
}
```

```rust
/// Verifies that CivilDate::of returns an error, with the reason, when the day is 30 February.
/// Compared with: `NaiveDate::from_ymd_opt(2026, 2, 30)` returns `None` and gives no reason.
#[test]
fn returns_day_out_of_range_when_the_day_is_30_february() {
    // GIVEN: 30 February 2026
    let given_year = 2026;
    let given_month = 2;
    let given_day = 30;

    // WHEN
    let actual_result = CivilDate::of(given_year, given_month, given_day);

    // EXPECTATIONS: no date, as chrono finds too, because February 2026 has 28 days
    let expected_is_err = NaiveDate::from_ymd_opt(2026, 2, 30).is_none();
    let expected_codes = vec!["day-out-of-range"];

    // THEN
    assert_eq!(expected_is_err, actual_result.is_err());
    assert_eq!(expected_codes, actual_result.unwrap_err().codes());
}
```

## 4. Adding

### 5 Nov + 30 days

**C#**

```csharp
/// <summary>

}
```

### Which comes first

**C#**

```csharp
/// <summary>
/// Verifies that CivilDate's less-than operator is true when the left date comes first.
/// Compared with: <c>DateOnly</c>'s operator gives the same answer. Plain dates always have an order.
/// </summary>
[Fact]
public void Test_LessThan_ReturnsTrue_WhenTheLeftDateComesFirst()
{
    // GIVEN: Christmas Day 2026
    CivilDate givenChristmas = CivilDate.Of(2026, 12, 25);

    // SYSTEM UNDER TEST: 5 November 2026
    CivilDate sut = CivilDate.Of(2026, 11, 5);

    // WHEN
    bool actualComesFirst = sut < givenChristmas;

    // EXPECTATIONS: .NET's answer for the same two days
    bool expectedComesFirst = new DateOnly(2026, 11, 5) < new DateOnly(2026, 12, 25);

    // THEN
    Assert.Equal(expectedComesFirst, actualComesFirst);
}

/// <summary>
/// Verifies that TemporalContext.Compare returns both orders when both wall times fall in the same overlap.
/// Compared with: two <c>DateTime</c> values of Kind Unspecified compare by wall time and always say "earlier".
/// </summary>
[Fact]
public void Test_Compare_ReturnsMultiple_WhenBothWallTimesFallInAnOverlap()
{
    // GIVEN: a call at 01:30 and a stand-up at 01:45, on the night New York's clocks go back from 02:00 to 01:00
    ZonedIntent givenCall = CivilDateTime.Of(2026, 11, 1, 1, 30).InZone("America/New_York");
    ZonedIntent givenStandup = CivilDateTime.Of(2026, 11, 1, 1, 45).InZone("America/New_York");

    // SETUP: the pinned demo zone rules, never this machine's tz database
    ZoneRules envRules = Fixtures.DemoZoneRules();

    // SYSTEM UNDER TEST
    TemporalContext sut = TemporalContext.With(envRules);

    // WHEN
    Outcome<Ordering> actualOutcome = sut.Compare(givenCall, givenStandup);

    // EXPECTATIONS: either could come first (01:30 standard time is after 01:45 daylight time)
    UtvStatus expectedStatus = UtvStatus.Multiple;
    string expectedCode = "ambiguous";

    // THEN
    Assert.Equal(expectedStatus, actualOutcome.Status);
    Assert.Contains(expectedCode, actualOutcome.Diagnostics.Codes);
}
```

```rust
    // GIVEN: Christmas Day 2026
    let given_christmas = CivilDate::of(2026, 12, 25)?;

    // SYSTEM UNDER TEST: 5 November 2026
    let sut = CivilDate::of(2026, 11, 5)?;

    // WHEN
    let actual_comes_first = sut < given_christmas;

    // EXPECTATIONS: chrono's answer for the same two days
    let expected_comes_first = NaiveDate::from_ymd_opt(2026, 11, 5).unwrap() < NaiveDate::from_ymd_opt(2026, 12, 25).unwrap();

    // THEN
    assert_eq!(expected_comes_first, actual_comes_first);
    Ok(())
}

/// Verifies that TemporalContext::compare returns both orders when both wall times fall in the same overlap.
/// Compared with: two `NaiveDateTime`s compare by wall time and always say "earlier"; two chrono-tz
/// `DateTime`s can't even be made until `LocalResult::earliest` or `latest` has picked an instant for each.
#[test]
fn returns_multiple_when_both_wall_times_fall_in_an_overlap() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
    // GIVEN: a call at 01:30 and a stand-up at 01:45, on the night New York's clocks go back from 02:00 to 01:00
    let given_call = CivilDateTime::of(2026, 11, 1, 1, 30)?.in_zone("America/New_York");
    let given_standup = CivilDateTime::of(2026, 11, 1, 1, 45)?.in_zone("America/New_York");

    // SETUP: the pinned demo zone rules, never this machine's tz database
    let env_rules = demo_zone_rules();

    // SYSTEM UNDER TEST
    let sut = TemporalContext::with(env_rules);

    // WHEN
    let actual_outcome = sut.compare(&given_call, &given_standup);

    // EXPECTATIONS: either could come first (01:30 standard time is after 01:45 daylight time)
    let expected_orders = vec![Ordering::Less, Ordering::Greater];
    let expected_code = "ambiguous";

    // THEN
    match actual_outcome {
        Outcome::Multiple(actual_orders, actual_diagnostics) => {
            assert_eq!(expected_orders, actual_orders);
            assert!(actual_diagnostics.contains(expected_code));
        }
        other => panic!("expected both orders, got {other:?}"),
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

## 7. Parsing with offsets

### Z vs +00:00

**C#**

```csharp
/// <summary>
/// Verifies that Temporal.Parse returns an Instant when the text ends in Z.
/// Compared with: <c>DateTimeOffset.Parse</c> gives an offset of +00:00, the same as for the text "+00:00".
/// </summary>
[Fact]
public void Test_Parse_ReturnsAnInstant_WhenTheTextEndsInZ()
{
    // GIVEN: 14:30 UTC, written with Z: a moment, with no local wall time implied
    string givenText = "2026-11-05T14:30:00Z";

    // WHEN
    Outcome<ITemporalValue> actualOutcome = Temporal.Parse(givenText);

    // EXPECTATIONS: the moment .NET parses from the same text
    Instant expectedInstant = Instant.FromDateTimeOffset(DateTimeOffset.Parse("2026-11-05T14:30:00Z", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture));

    // THEN
    Instant actualInstant = Assert.IsType<Instant>(actualOutcome.Single());
    Assert.Equal(expectedInstant, actualInstant);
}

/// <summary>
/// Verifies that Temporal.Parse returns a FixedOffsetDateTime when the text ends in +00:00.
/// Compared with: <c>DateTimeOffset.Parse</c> cannot tell this text from the one ending in Z.
/// </summary>
[Fact]
public void Test_Parse_ReturnsAFixedOffsetDateTime_WhenTheTextEndsInPlusZero()
{
    // GIVEN: 14:30 at offset +00:00: a wall time somewhere that is at UTC+0 right now
    string givenText = "2026-11-05T14:30:00+00:00";

    // WHEN
    Outcome<ITemporalValue> actualOutcome = Temporal.Parse(givenText);

    // EXPECTATIONS: the value .NET parses from the same text, and the text kept as written
    FixedOffsetDateTime expectedDateTime =
        FixedOffsetDateTime.FromDateTimeOffset(DateTimeOffset.Parse("2026-11-05T14:30:00+00:00", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture));
    string expectedText = "2026-11-05T14:30:00+00:00";

    // THEN
    FixedOffsetDateTime actualDateTime = Assert.IsType<FixedOffsetDateTime>(actualOutcome.Single());
    Assert.Equal(expectedDateTime, actualDateTime);
    Assert.Equal(expectedText, actualDateTime.ToString());
}
```

## 8. Time zones

### 09:00 in Paris, seen from New York

**C#**

```csharp
/// <summary>
/// Verifies that Instant.InZone returns the wall time and offset in the zone when the zone has rules for it.
/// Compared with: <c>TimeZoneInfo.ConvertTimeFromUtc</c> gives the same wall time from this machine's tz database.
/// </summary>
[Fact]
public void Test_InZone_ReturnsTheLocalWallTime_WhenTheZoneHasRules()
{
    // GIVEN: New York
    string givenZoneId = "America/New_York";

    // SETUP: the pinned demo zone rules, never this machine's tz database
    TemporalContext envContext = TemporalContext.With(Fixtures.DemoZoneRules());

    // SYSTEM UNDER TEST: 07:00 UTC on 1 June 2027, when the meeting starts in Paris
    Instant sut = Instant.FromDateTimeOffset(new DateTimeOffset(2027, 6, 1, 7, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero));

    // WHEN
    Outcome<ZonedIntent> actualOutcome = sut.InZone(givenZoneId, envContext);

    // EXPECTATIONS: the wall time .NET computes, with the offset UTV asserts alongside it
    TimeZoneInfo tmpNewYork = TimeZoneInfo.FindSystemTimeZoneById("America/New_York");
    DateTime tmpWallTime = TimeZoneInfo.ConvertTimeFromUtc(new DateTime(2027, 6, 1, 7, 0, 0, DateTimeKind.Utc), tmpNewYork);
    CivilDateTime expectedWallTime = CivilDateTime.FromDateTime(tmpWallTime).Single();
    string expectedText = "2027-06-01T03:00:00-04:00[America/New_York]";

    // THEN
    Assert.Equal(expectedWallTime, actualOutcome.Single().DateTime);
    Assert.Equal(expectedText, actualOutcome.Single().ToString());
}

/// <summary>
/// Verifies that ZonedIntent.Resolve returns the one instant when the wall time happens exactly once.
/// Compared with: <c>TimeZoneInfo.ConvertTimeToUtc</c> finds the same instant in this machine's tz database.
/// </summary>
[Fact]
public void Test_Resolve_ReturnsTheInstant_WhenTheWallTimeHappensOnce()
{
    // SETUP: the pinned demo zone rules, never this machine's tz database
    TemporalContext envContext = TemporalContext.With(Fixtures.DemoZoneRules());

    // SYSTEM UNDER TEST: a meeting at 09:00 on 1 June 2027 in Paris
    ZonedIntent sut = CivilDateTime.Of(2027, 6, 1, 9, 0).InZone("Europe/Paris");

    // WHEN
    Outcome<Instant> actualOutcome = sut.Resolve(envContext);

    // EXPECTATIONS: the instant .NET finds for the same wall time
    TimeZoneInfo tmpParis = TimeZoneInfo.FindSystemTimeZoneById("Europe/Paris");
    DateTime tmpUtc = TimeZoneInfo.ConvertTimeToUtc(new DateTime(2027, 6, 1, 9, 0, 0), tmpParis);
    Instant expectedInstant = Instant.FromDateTimeOffset(new DateTimeOffset(tmpUtc));

    // THEN
    Assert.Equal(expectedInstant, actualOutcome.Single());
}
```

```typescript
  }).formatToParts(Date.UTC(2027, 5, 1, 7, 0));
  const tmpFields = Object.fromEntries(tmpParts.map((part) => [part.type, part.value]));
  const expectedWallTime = CivilDateTime.of(

    Number(tmpFields["hour"]), Number(tmpFields["minute"]), Number(tmpFields["second"]));

/**
 * Verifies that ZonedIntent.resolve returns the one instant when the wall time happens exactly once.
 * Compared with: JavaScript has no call for this; subtracting the offset `Intl.DateTimeFormat` reports for Paris
 * (from the host's tz database) gives the same instant.
 */
it("returns the instant when the wall time happens once", () => {
  // SETUP: the pinned demo zone rules, never the host's tz database
  const envContext = TemporalContext.with(demoZoneRules());

  // SYSTEM UNDER TEST: a meeting at 09:00 on 1 June 2027 in Paris
  const sut: ZonedIntent = CivilDateTime.of(2027, 6, 1, 9, 0).inZone("Europe/Paris");

  // WHEN
  const actualOutcome: Outcome<Instant> = sut.resolve(envContext);

  // EXPECTATIONS: 09:00 minus the offset Intl reports for Paris that morning ("GMT+02:00")
  const tmpWallTimeAsUtc = Date.UTC(2027, 5, 1, 9, 0);
  const tmpOffsetName = new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { timeZone: "Europe/Paris", timeZoneName: "longOffset" })
    .formatToParts(tmpWallTimeAsUtc).find((part) => part.type === "timeZoneName")?.value;
  const expectedInstant = Instant.fromUnixMilliseconds(tmpWallTimeAsUtc - Number(tmpOffsetName?.slice(3, 6)) * 3_600_000);

  // THEN
  assert.equal(String(actualOutcome.single()), String(expectedInstant));
});
```

```csharp
/// <summary>
/// Verifies that ZonedIntent.Resolve returns none when the wall time falls in a daylight-saving gap.

/// </summary>
[Fact]
public void Test_Resolve_ReturnsNone_WhenTheWallTimeFallsInAGap()
{
    // SETUP: the pinned demo zone rules, never this machine's tz database
    TemporalContext envContext = TemporalContext.With(Fixtures.DemoZoneRules());

    // SYSTEM UNDER TEST: 02:30 on 8 March 2026 in New York, when clocks jump from 02:00 to 03:00
    ZonedIntent sut = CivilDateTime.Of(2026, 3, 8, 2, 30).InZone("America/New_York");

    // WHEN
    Outcome<Instant> actualOutcome = sut.Resolve(envContext);

    // EXPECTATIONS: no such instant, explained by the gap diagnostic
    UtvStatus expectedStatus = UtvStatus.None;
    string expectedCode = "gap";

    // THEN

    Assert.Contains(expectedCode, actualOutcome.Diagnostics.Codes);

/// <summary>
/// Verifies that ZonedIntent.Resolve with Gap.ShiftForward moves the wall time forward by the length of the gap.
/// Compared with: .NET has no such policy; it throws instead (see TimeZoneInfoTests).
/// </summary>
[Fact]
public void Test_Resolve_ShiftsForwardByTheGap_WhenShiftForwardIsRequested()
{
    // GIVEN: the policy that moves a skipped wall time forward by the gap
    Gap givenPolicy = Gap.ShiftForward;

    // SETUP: the pinned demo zone rules, never this machine's tz database
    TemporalContext envContext = TemporalContext.With(Fixtures.DemoZoneRules());

    // SYSTEM UNDER TEST: 02:30 on 8 March 2026 in New York, when clocks jump from 02:00 to 03:00
    ZonedIntent sut = CivilDateTime.Of(2026, 3, 8, 2, 30).InZone("America/New_York");

    // WHEN
    Outcome<Instant> actualOutcome = sut.Resolve(envContext, givenPolicy);

    // EXPECTATIONS: 03:30 daylight time, four hours behind UTC
    Instant expectedInstant = Instant.FromDateTimeOffset(new DateTimeOffset(2026, 3, 8, 3, 30, 0, TimeSpan.FromHours(-4)));

    // THEN
    Assert.Equal(expectedInstant, actualOutcome.Single());
}
```

## 10. DST overlap

### 01:30 on 1 November 2026 in New York

**C#**

```csharp
/// <summary>
/// Verifies that ZonedIntent.Resolve returns both instants when the wall time happens twice.
/// Compared with: <c>TimeZoneInfo.ConvertTimeToUtc</c> silently picks one of them, the standard-time one.
/// </summary>
[Fact]
public void Test_Resolve_ReturnsBothInstants_WhenTheWallTimeFallsInAnOverlap()
{
    // SETUP: the pinned demo zone rules, never this machine's tz database
    TemporalContext envContext = TemporalContext.With(Fixtures.DemoZoneRules());

    // SYSTEM UNDER TEST: 01:30 on 1 November 2026 in New York, when clocks go back from 02:00 to 01:00
    ZonedIntent sut = CivilDateTime.Of(2026, 11, 1, 1, 30).InZone("America/New_York");

    // WHEN
    Outcome<Instant> actualOutcome = sut.Resolve(envContext);

    // EXPECTATIONS: 01:30 daylight time, then 01:30 standard time; .NET's single answer is one of them
    Instant[] expectedInstants =
    {
        Instant.FromDateTimeOffset(new DateTimeOffset(2026, 11, 1, 1, 30, 0, TimeSpan.FromHours(-4))),
        Instant.FromDateTimeOffset(new DateTimeOffset(2026, 11, 1, 1, 30, 0, TimeSpan.FromHours(-5))),
    };
    string expectedCode = "ambiguous";
    TimeZoneInfo tmpNewYork = TimeZoneInfo.FindSystemTimeZoneById("America/New_York");
    DateTime tmpUtc = TimeZoneInfo.ConvertTimeToUtc(new DateTime(2026, 11, 1, 1, 30, 0), tmpNewYork);
    Instant expectedNativePick = Instant.FromDateTimeOffset(new DateTimeOffset(tmpUtc));

    // THEN
    Outcome<Instant>.Multiple actualMultiple = Assert.IsType<Outcome<Instant>.Multiple>(actualOutcome);
    Assert.Equal(expectedInstants, actualMultiple.Values);
    Assert.Contains(expectedCode, actualOutcome.Diagnostics.Codes);
    Assert.Contains(expectedNativePick, actualMultiple.Values);
}

/// <summary>
/// Verifies that ZonedIntent.Resolve with Overlap.Earliest returns the first of the two instants.
/// Compared with: <c>TimeZoneInfo.ConvertTimeToUtc</c> picks the later one, and does not say so.
/// </summary>
[Fact]
public void Test_Resolve_ReturnsTheEarlierInstant_WhenEarliestIsRequested()
{
    // GIVEN: the policy that picks the earlier of two instants
    Overlap givenPolicy = Overlap.Earliest;

    // SETUP: the pinned demo zone rules, never this machine's tz database
    TemporalContext envContext = TemporalContext.With(Fixtures.DemoZoneRules());

    // SYSTEM UNDER TEST: 01:30 on 1 November 2026 in New York, when clocks go back from 02:00 to 01:00
    ZonedIntent sut = CivilDateTime.Of(2026, 11, 1, 1, 30).InZone("America/New_York");

    // WHEN
    Outcome<Instant> actualOutcome = sut.Resolve(envContext, givenPolicy);

    // EXPECTATIONS: 01:30 daylight time, the first time the clock shows it
    Instant expectedInstant = Instant.FromDateTimeOffset(new DateTimeOffset(2026, 11, 1, 1, 30, 0, TimeSpan.FromHours(-4)));

    // THEN
    Assert.Equal(expectedInstant, actualOutcome.Single());
}
```

```python
        from_native(datetime(2026, 11, 1, 1, 30, tzinfo=timezone(timedelta(hours=-5))), Intent.INSTANT).single(),
    )
    expected_code = "ambiguous"
    tmp_utc = datetime(2026, 11, 1, 1, 30, tzinfo=ZoneInfo("America/New_York")).astimezone(timezone.utc)
    expected_native_pick = from_native(tmp_utc, Intent.INSTANT).single()

    # THEN
    self.assertIsInstance(actual_outcome, expected_outcome_type)
    self.assertEqual(expected_instants, actual_outcome.values)
    self.assertIn(expected_code, actual_outcome.codes)
    self.assertIn(expected_native_pick, actual_outcome.values)

def test_returns_the_earlier_instant_when_earliest_is_requested(self):
    """Verifies that ZonedIntent.resolve with Overlap.EARLIEST returns the first of the two instants.

    Compared with: Python's default ``fold=0`` picks the same instant, and does not say there was a choice.
    """
    # GIVEN: the policy that picks the earlier of two instants
    given_policy = ResolutionPolicy(overlap=Overlap.EARLIEST)

    # SETUP: the pinned demo zone rules, never this machine's tz database
    env_context = TemporalContext(demo_zone_rules())

    # SYSTEM UNDER TEST: 01:30 on 1 November 2026 in New York, when clocks go back from 02:00 to 01:00
    sut = CivilDateTime.of(2026, 11, 1, 1, 30).in_zone("America/New_York")

    # WHEN
    actual_outcome = sut.resolve(env_context, given_policy)

    # EXPECTATIONS: 01:30 daylight time, the instant Python picks with fold=0
    tmp_utc = datetime(2026, 11, 1, 1, 30, fold=0, tzinfo=ZoneInfo("America/New_York")).astimezone(timezone.utc)
    expected_instant = from_native(tmp_utc, Intent.INSTANT).single()

    # THEN
    self.assertEqual(expected_instant, actual_outcome.single())
```

```rust
/// Compared with: chrono-tz's `with_ymd_and_hms` returns `LocalResult::Ambiguous` with the same two instants;
/// chrono is the one standard API that reports both.
#[test]
fn returns_both_instants_when_the_wall_time_falls_in_an_overlap() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
    // SETUP: the pinned demo zone rules, never this machine's tz database
    let env_context = TemporalContext::with(demo_zone_rules());

    // SYSTEM UNDER TEST: 01:30 on 1 November 2026 in New York, when clocks go back from 02:00 to 01:00
    let sut = CivilDateTime::of(2026, 11, 1, 1, 30)?.in_zone("America/New_York");

    // WHEN

    // EXPECTATIONS: 01:30 daylight time, then 01:30 standard time, as chrono-tz finds them
    let tmp_native = New_York.with_ymd_and_hms(2026, 11, 1, 1, 30, 0);
    let expected_instants = vec![
        Instant::try_from(tmp_native.earliest().unwrap().with_timezone(&Utc))?,
        Instant::try_from(tmp_native.latest().unwrap().with_timezone(&Utc))?,
    ];
    let expected_code = "ambiguous";

    // THEN
    match actual_outcome {
        Outcome::Multiple(actual_instants, actual_diagnostics) => {
            assert_eq!(expected_instants, actual_instants);
            assert!(actual_diagnostics.contains(expected_code));
        }
        other => panic!("expected both instants, got {other:?}"),
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

## 11. Timestamps

### Exact fractions and differences

**C#**

```csharp
/// <summary>
/// Verifies that Instant.Until returns the exact number of seconds, as a fraction, between two instants.
/// Compared with: subtracting two <c>DateTimeOffset</c> values gives a <c>TimeSpan</c> whose TotalSeconds is a double.
/// </summary>
[Fact]
public void Test_Until_ReturnsAnExactFraction_WhenTheInstantsAreAFractionOfASecondApart()
{
    // GIVEN: one hour, 0.75 seconds later
    Instant givenLater = Instant.FromUnixSeconds(1_793_889_001);

    // SYSTEM UNDER TEST: 13:30:00.25 on 5 November 2026
    Instant sut = Instant.FromUnixSeconds(1_793_885_400, 250_000_000);

    // WHEN
    PosixSeconds actualSeconds = sut.Until(givenLater);

    // EXPECTATIONS: exactly 14403/4 seconds, the number .NET approximates as a double
    PosixSeconds expectedSeconds = PosixSeconds.Of(14_403, 4);
    double expectedApproximation =
        (DateTimeOffset.FromUnixTimeSeconds(1_793_889_001) - DateTimeOffset.FromUnixTimeMilliseconds(1_793_885_400_250)).TotalSeconds;

    // THEN
    Assert.Equal(expectedSeconds, actualSeconds);
    Assert.Equal(expectedApproximation, (double)actualSeconds.Numerator / (double)actualSeconds.Denominator);
}
```

```java
 */

    Instant sut = Instant.fromUnixSeconds(1_793_885_400, 250_000_000);

    // WHEN

    Duration tmpNative = Duration.between(java.time.Instant.ofEpochMilli(1_793_885_400_250L), java.time.Instant.ofEpochSecond(1_793_889_001));
    PosixSeconds expectedSeconds = PosixSeconds.from(tmpNative);
    String expectedText = "3600.75 s (POSIX)";

    // THEN

    assertEquals(expectedText, actualSeconds.toString());
}
```

```rust
/// Verifies that Instant::until returns the exact number of seconds, as a fraction, between two instants.
/// Compared with: subtracting two `DateTime<Utc>`s gives a `TimeDelta` of the same length, exact to the
/// nanosecond; `TimeDelta::seconds(1) / 3` shows where that stops, while `PosixSeconds::of_ratio(1, 3)` is exact.
#[test]
fn returns_an_exact_fraction_when_the_instants_are_a_fraction_of_a_second_apart() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
    // GIVEN: one hour and 0.75 seconds later
    let given_later = Instant::from_unix_seconds(1_793_889_001);

    // SYSTEM UNDER TEST: 13:30:00.25 on 5 November 2026
    let sut = Instant::from_unix_seconds_nanos(1_793_885_400, 250_000_000);

    // WHEN
    let actual_seconds = sut.until(given_later);

    // EXPECTATIONS: exactly 14403/4 seconds, the length chrono's TimeDelta gives in nanoseconds
    let tmp_delta = DateTime::from_timestamp(1_793_889_001, 0).unwrap() - DateTime::from_timestamp(1_793_885_400, 250_000_000).unwrap();
    let expected_seconds = PosixSeconds::of_ratio(tmp_delta.num_nanoseconds().unwrap().into(), 1_000_000_000)?;
    let expected_text = "3600.75 s (POSIX)";

    // THEN
    assert_eq!(expected_seconds, actual_seconds);
    assert_eq!(expected_text, actual_seconds.to_string());
    Ok(())
}
```

```csharp
/// <summary>
/// Verifies that Instant.Add with SI seconds returns unsupported when no leap-second table is available.
/// Compared with: <c>TimeSpan</c> has one kind of second, so .NET cannot tell SI seconds from POSIX seconds.
/// </summary>
[Fact]
public void Test_Add_ReturnsUnsupported_WhenGivenSiSecondsWithoutALeapSecondTable()
{
    // GIVEN: 86,400 SI seconds, as a physicist measures a day
    ElapsedSeconds givenSeconds = ElapsedSeconds.Of(86_400);

    // SYSTEM UNDER TEST: noon on 7 March 2026 in New York
    Instant sut = Instant.FromDateTimeOffset(new DateTimeOffset(2026, 3, 7, 12, 0, 0, TimeSpan.FromHours(-5)));

    // WHEN
    Outcome<Instant> actualOutcome = sut.Add(givenSeconds);

    // EXPECTATIONS: unsupported, because SI seconds on a POSIX timescale need leap seconds
    UtvStatus expectedStatus = UtvStatus.Unsupported;
    string expectedCode = "needs-leap-seconds";

    // THEN
    Assert.Equal(expectedStatus, actualOutcome.Status);
    Assert.Contains(expectedCode, actualOutcome.Diagnostics.Codes);
}

/// <summary>
/// Verifies that ZonedIntent.AddDays keeps the wall time when the day crosses a daylight-saving change.
/// Compared with: <c>DateTimeOffset.AddDays</c> keeps the offset instead, so the wall time moves to 13:00.
/// </summary>
[Fact]
public void Test_AddDays_KeepsTheWallTime_WhenTheDayCrossesADstChange()
{
    // GIVEN: one calendar day
    int givenDays = 1;

    // SYSTEM UNDER TEST: noon on 7 March 2026 in New York, the day before clocks spring forward
    ZonedIntent sut = CivilDateTime.Of(2026, 3, 7, 12, 0).InZone("America/New_York");

    // WHEN
    ZonedIntent actualNextNoon = sut.AddDays(givenDays);

    // EXPECTATIONS: noon again, on the next date
    ZonedIntent expectedNextNoon = CivilDateTime.Of(2026, 3, 8, 12, 0).InZone("America/New_York");

    // THEN
    Assert.Equal(expectedNextNoon, actualNextNoon);
}
```

## 13. Ranges

### November, open-ended and unknown ends

**C#**

```csharp
/// <summary>
/// Verifies that a half-open Interval definitely contains a day between its ends.
/// Compared with: <c>day &gt;= first &amp;&amp; day &lt; end</c> on <c>DateOnly</c> values says the same.
/// </summary>
[Fact]
public void Test_HalfOpen_DefinitelyContainsTheDay_WhenTheDayIsBetweenTheEnds()
{
    // GIVEN: 15 November 2026
    CivilDate givenDay = CivilDate.Of(2026, 11, 15);

    // SYSTEM UNDER TEST: November 2026, from the 1st up to but not including 1 December
    Interval<CivilDate> sut = Interval.HalfOpen(CivilDate.Of(2026, 11, 1), CivilDate.Of(2026, 12, 1));

    // WHEN
    Truth actualContains = sut.Contains(givenDay);

    // EXPECTATIONS: the answer .NET's hand-written bounds give
    DateOnly tmpDay = new(2026, 11, 15);
    bool tmpNativeContains = tmpDay >= new DateOnly(2026, 11, 1) && tmpDay < new DateOnly(2026, 12, 1);
    Truth expectedContains = tmpNativeContains ? Truth.Definitely : Truth.Impossible;

    // THEN
    Assert.Equal(expectedContains, actualContains);
}

/// <summary>
/// Verifies that a half-open Interval cannot contain its excluded end.
/// Compared with: the hand-written <c>day &lt; end</c> excludes it too, if nobody writes <c>&lt;=</c> by mistake.
/// </summary>
[Fact]
public void Test_HalfOpen_CannotContainTheDay_WhenTheDayIsTheExcludedEnd()
{
    // GIVEN: 1 December 2026, the end of the interval
    CivilDate givenDay = CivilDate.Of(2026, 12, 1);

    // SYSTEM UNDER TEST: November 2026, from the 1st up to but not including 1 December
    Interval<CivilDate> sut = Interval.HalfOpen(CivilDate.Of(2026, 11, 1), CivilDate.Of(2026, 12, 1));

    // WHEN
    Truth actualContains = sut.Contains(givenDay);

    // EXPECTATIONS: impossible, and written with the end's bracket open
    Truth expectedContains = Truth.Impossible;
    string expectedText = "[2026-11-01, 2026-12-01)";

    // THEN
    Assert.Equal(expectedContains, actualContains);
    Assert.Equal(expectedText, sut.ToString());
}

/// <summary>
/// Verifies that an Interval with an unknown end only possibly contains a later day.
/// Compared with: the same <c>null</c> end would be read as "no end", and the answer would wrongly be "yes".

[Fact]
public void Test_Of_PossiblyContainsALaterDay_WhenTheEndIsUnknown()
{
    // GIVEN: 1 June 2027
    CivilDate givenDay = CivilDate.Of(2027, 6, 1);

    // SYSTEM UNDER TEST: from 1 November 2026, until an end nobody knows yet
    Interval<CivilDate> sut = Interval.Of(Bound.Included(CivilDate.Of(2026, 11, 1)), Bound.Unknown);

    // WHEN
    Truth actualContains = sut.Contains(givenDay);

    // EXPECTATIONS: possibly, and written with "?" for the unknown end
    Truth expectedContains = Truth.Possibly;
    string expectedText = "[2026-11-01, ?)";

    // THEN
    Assert.Equal(expectedContains, actualContains);
    Assert.Equal(expectedText, sut.ToString());
}
```

```rust
/// Verifies that a half-open Interval definitely contains a day between its ends.
/// Compared with: `(nov1..dec1).contains(&day)` on `NaiveDate`s says the same.
#[test]
fn definitely_contains_the_day_when_the_day_is_between_the_ends() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
    // GIVEN: 15 November 2026
    let given_day = CivilDate::of(2026, 11, 15)?;

    // SYSTEM UNDER TEST: November 2026, from the 1st up to but not including 1 December
    let sut = Interval::half_open(CivilDate::of(2026, 11, 1)?, CivilDate::of(2026, 12, 1)?)?;

    // WHEN
    let actual_contains = sut.contains(&given_day);

    // EXPECTATIONS: the answer std's half-open range gives
    let tmp_november = NaiveDate::from_ymd_opt(2026, 11, 1).unwrap()..NaiveDate::from_ymd_opt(2026, 12, 1).unwrap();
    let tmp_native_contains = tmp_november.contains(&NaiveDate::from_ymd_opt(2026, 11, 15).unwrap());
    let expected_contains = if tmp_native_contains { Truth::Definitely } else { Truth::Impossible };

    // THEN
    assert_eq!(expected_contains, actual_contains);
    Ok(())
}

/// Verifies that a half-open Interval cannot contain its excluded end.
/// Compared with: `(nov1..dec1).contains(&dec1)` is false too.
#[test]
fn cannot_contain_the_day_when_the_day_is_the_excluded_end() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
    // GIVEN: 1 December 2026, the end of the interval
    let given_day = CivilDate::of(2026, 12, 1)?;

    // SYSTEM UNDER TEST: November 2026, from the 1st up to but not including 1 December
    let sut = Interval::half_open(CivilDate::of(2026, 11, 1)?, CivilDate::of(2026, 12, 1)?)?;

    // WHEN
    let actual_contains = sut.contains(&given_day);

    // EXPECTATIONS: impossible, and written with the end's bracket open
    let expected_contains = Truth::Impossible;
    let expected_text = "[2026-11-01, 2026-12-01)";

    // THEN
    assert_eq!(expected_contains, actual_contains);
    assert_eq!(expected_text, sut.to_string());
    Ok(())
}

/// Verifies that an Interval with an unknown end only possibly contains a later day.
/// Compared with: std has no range with an unknown end; an `Option<NaiveDate>` end of `None` has to be read as
/// `nov1..` (no end), and the answer would wrongly be "yes".
#[test]
fn possibly_contains_a_later_day_when_the_end_is_unknown() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
    // GIVEN: 1 June 2027
    let given_day = CivilDate::of(2027, 6, 1)?;

    // SYSTEM UNDER TEST: from 1 November 2026, until an end nobody knows yet
    let sut = Interval::of(Bound::Included(CivilDate::of(2026, 11, 1)?), Bound::Unknown)?;

    // WHEN
    let actual_contains = sut.contains(&given_day);

    // EXPECTATIONS: possibly, and "?" written for the unknown end
    let expected_contains = Truth::Possibly;
    let expected_text = "[2026-11-01, ?)";

    // THEN
    assert_eq!(expected_contains, actual_contains);
    assert_eq!(expected_text, sut.to_string());
    Ok(())
}
```

## 14. Round trip

### Native → UTV → native

**C#**

```csharp
/// <summary>
/// Verifies that FixedOffsetDateTime.ToDateTimeOffset gives back exactly the native value it was made from.
/// Compared with: <c>DateTimeOffset.EqualsExact</c> checks the instant and the offset.
/// </summary>
[Fact]
public void Test_ToDateTimeOffset_ReturnsTheOriginal_WhenTheValueCameFromADateTimeOffset()
{
    // GIVEN: lunch at 14:30 on 5 November 2026, one hour east of UTC
    DateTimeOffset givenLunch = new(2026, 11, 5, 14, 30, 0, TimeSpan.FromHours(1));

    // SYSTEM UNDER TEST: the same lunch as a UTV value
    FixedOffsetDateTime sut = FixedOffsetDateTime.FromDateTimeOffset(givenLunch);

    // WHEN
    Outcome<DateTimeOffset> actualOutcome = sut.ToDateTimeOffset();

    // EXPECTATIONS: the very same native value
    DateTimeOffset expectedLunch = new(2026, 11, 5, 14, 30, 0, TimeSpan.FromHours(1));

    // THEN
    Assert.True(expectedLunch.EqualsExact(actualOutcome.Single()));
}
```

```java
/**
 * Verifies that FixedOffsetDateTime.toOffsetDateTime gives back exactly the native value when the value came
 * from an OffsetDateTime.
 * Compared with: {@code OffsetDateTime.equals} checks the wall time and the offset, not just the instant.
 */
@Test
void returnsTheOriginal_whenTheValueCameFromAnOffsetDateTime() {
    // GIVEN: lunch at 14:30 on 5 November 2026, one hour east of UTC
    OffsetDateTime givenLunch = OffsetDateTime.of(2026, 11, 5, 14, 30, 0, 0, ZoneOffset.ofHours(1));

    // SYSTEM UNDER TEST: the same lunch as a UTV value
    FixedOffsetDateTime sut = FixedOffsetDateTime.from(givenLunch);

    // WHEN
    Outcome<OffsetDateTime> actualOutcome = sut.toOffsetDateTime();

    // EXPECTATIONS: the very same native value
    OffsetDateTime expectedLunch = OffsetDateTime.of(2026, 11, 5, 14, 30, 0, 0, ZoneOffset.ofHours(1));

    // THEN
    assertEquals(expectedLunch, actualOutcome.single());
}
```

```python
def test_returns_the_original_when_the_value_came_from_a_datetime(self):
    """Verifies that to_native gives back exactly the native value a FixedOffsetDateTime was made from.

    Compared with: ``datetime``'s ``==`` compares the moments, so the offset is checked as well.
    """
    # GIVEN: lunch at 14:30 on 5 November 2026, one hour east of UTC
    given_lunch = datetime(2026, 11, 5, 14, 30, tzinfo=timezone(timedelta(hours=1)))

    # SYSTEM UNDER TEST: the same lunch as a UTV value, with its intent named
    sut = from_native(given_lunch, Intent.OFFSET).single()

    # WHEN
    actual_outcome = to_native(sut)

    # EXPECTATIONS: the very same native value
    expected_lunch = datetime(2026, 11, 5, 14, 30, tzinfo=timezone(timedelta(hours=1)))

    # THEN
    self.assertEqual(expected_lunch, actual_outcome.single())
    self.assertEqual(expected_lunch.utcoffset(), actual_outcome.single().utcoffset())
```

```rust
/// Verifies that converting a FixedOffsetDateTime into a `DateTime<FixedOffset>` gives back exactly the native
/// value it was made from.
/// Compared with: chrono's `==` on `DateTime` compares only the instant, so the offset is compared on its own.
#[test]
fn returns_the_original_when_the_value_came_from_a_date_time() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
    // GIVEN: lunch at 14:30 on 5 November 2026, one hour east of UTC
    let given_lunch = DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339("2026-11-05T14:30:00+01:00")?;

    // SYSTEM UNDER TEST: the same lunch as a UTV value
    let sut = FixedOffsetDateTime::try_from(given_lunch)?;

    // WHEN
    let actual_result: Result<DateTime<FixedOffset>, Diagnostics> = sut.try_into();

    // EXPECTATIONS: the very same native value, instant and offset
    let expected_lunch = DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339("2026-11-05T14:30:00+01:00")?;
    let expected_offset = FixedOffset::east_opt(3600).unwrap();

    // THEN
    let actual_lunch = actual_result?;
    assert_eq!(expected_lunch, actual_lunch);
    assert_eq!(expected_offset, *actual_lunch.offset());
    Ok(())
}
```
